Josh Shapiro

Democratic candidate for Governor and Lieutenant Governor, Pennsylvania · Incumbent

Governor of Pennsylvania (incumbent)

Josh Shapiro is the Democratic governor of Pennsylvania, in office since January 2023, and is running for re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election. He previously served as Pennsylvania Attorney General, as a Montgomery County commissioner and as a state representative. His general-election opponents are Republican state Treasurer Stacy Garrity and Libertarian Ken Krawchuk.

Where Shapiro stands

Skill games / gaming revenue
Supports taxing skill games at about the same rate as casino slot machines, roughly 50%. He would send the revenue to the state and says a large share should go to mass transit across Pennsylvania.
Gas prices / gas tax
Says he is open to suspending the state gas tax but that it is up to the legislature to bring up the measure. He blames high gas costs on federal tariffs and the war in Iran.
Medicaid / health care
Says every state is dealing with the upcoming federal Medicaid cuts and that no state can make up for the loss of federal funds.
Public education funding
Defends his administration's increases in education spending, including free school breakfast, more vo-tech opportunities and school mental health counseling. He says graduation rates are up and truancy is down.
School vouchers / school choice
Says he is still open to school vouchers. He says the voucher program he vetoed in 2023 did not have agreement from both the Democratic House and the Republican Senate.
Federal private-school scholarship tax credit
Has not decided whether Pennsylvania will opt into the federal scholarship tax-credit program created by the 2025 federal tax law. He says the state is reviewing it carefully.
State budget and spending
Defends his budgets and has asked his opponent which programs she would cut, naming free school breakfast and a 60% increase in apprenticeship funding as examples.
Minimum wage, gun laws, revenue proposals
Has sought a higher minimum wage, stricter gun laws, nondiscrimination protections for LGBTQ people, and new revenue, including legalizing recreational marijuana. The legislature has not passed these.

Background

  • Governor of Pennsylvania, 2023–present
  • Pennsylvania Attorney General, 2017–2023
  • Montgomery County Commissioner, 2012–2017
  • Pennsylvania House of Representatives, 2005–2012
  • Education: B.A., University of Rochester; J.D., Georgetown University Law Center
